topicTitle: Advanced Error Handling & Custom Error Classes

lessons.title: Subclassing the Native Error Object
lessons.description: Create custom error types by extending the built-in Error class for more meaningful error handling.

sections.heading: Why custom errors?
paragraphs: Native Error objects only carry a message. Custom error classes let you add properties, check error types, and handle different failure scenarios with specific logic.
list: Extend Error with class MyError extends Error
Add custom properties for extra context
Use instanceof to check error types in catch blocks

codeExamples.heading: Creating custom error classes
explanation: Custom errors extend Error and add domain-specific properties.
Use super(message) to call the parent Error constructor.
instanceof checks which specific error type was thrown.
This enables targeted error handling for different failure modes.

practice.task: Create a NetworkError class with status and url properties. Throw it when a fetch response is not ok and handle it specifically in a catch block.
hints: Check e instanceof NetworkError in the catch block.

keyTakeaways: Custom errors extend Error with domain-specific properties.
Use instanceof to check error types in catch blocks.
Custom errors make debugging easier with meaningful names and context.
Different error types enable different handling strategies.
lessons.challenge: Build an error hierarchy: AppError → NetworkError, ValidationError, AuthError. Each with unique properties and handling.

lessons.title: Building Domain Errors (ValidationError, NetworkError)
lessons.description: Design error classes for specific domains — API errors, validation errors and business logic errors.

sections.heading: Domain error patterns
list: Each domain error enables specific recovery logic

codeExamples.heading: Domain error classes
explanation: ApiError captures status, endpoint and retryability.
Domain-specific properties enable smart error handling.
Retryable errors (5xx) can be retried; client errors (4xx) cannot.
Error classes document your application's failure modes.

practice.task: Create a ValidationError class that stores field name, invalid value and validation rule. Throw it when form validation fails.

keyTakeaways: Domain errors capture the specific context of each failure type.
Properties like status, field and retryable enable smart recovery logic.
Error classes serve as documentation for your application's failure modes.
Always design errors with enough context for meaningful handling.
lessons.challenge: Build a complete error handling system for an e-commerce app with payment, inventory and auth error types.

lessons.title: Chaining Root Causes with Error Cause Properties
lessons.description: Preserve the original error when wrapping — the cause property tracks the full error chain.

sections.heading: Error cause chaining
paragraphs: When you catch an error and throw a new one, the original context is lost. The cause property (ES2022) preserves the original error, creating a chain of causation.
list: new Error(msg, { cause: originalError }) — preserves the root cause
Build chains: AppError → NetworkError → original TypeError
Essential for debugging complex error flows

codeExamples.heading: Error cause chaining
explanation: The cause option preserves the original error in the chain.
Access it with error.cause — it's a standard Error property.
You can chain multiple levels for deep error propagation.
This is invaluable for debugging production errors.

practice.task: Write a function that catches a network error and wraps it in a custom AppError, preserving the original error as the cause.
hints: Catch the original error and throw: new AppError(msg, { cause: originalError }).
In the outer catch, log both e.message and e.cause.message.
Verify the full chain is preserved.

keyTakeaways: The cause property preserves the original error when wrapping errors.
Access it with error.cause — it's a standard Error property.
Error chains help you trace complex error flows back to the root cause.
Always preserve the original error — never lose debugging context.
lessons.challenge: Build a 3-level error chain: database error → API error → user-facing error, each preserving the cause.
